tagline: West Africa's largest lagoon city — where boats already carry hundreds of thousands across the water each day, and a clean foiling tier is the obvious upgrade.
summary: Abidjan is built around the Ébrié Lagoon, a vast sheltered waterway that separates the business district of Le Plateau from Cocody, Treichville, Marcory and the port at Vridi. Lagoon transport is already deeply embedded: traditional pinasse water-taxis and the official Citrans/STL boats move very large daily volumes across a city where the bridges are chronically congested. Côte d'Ivoire has even launched modern electric-boat pilots on the lagoon. This is a proven, high-volume water-commuter market — and a clean, fast foiling tier is the natural premium upgrade over the diesel and pirogue fleet.
competitive_landscape: Unlike most markets, Abidjan has a mature lagoon-transport culture: informal pinasses, the municipal Citrans/SOTRA lagoon buses, and recently introduced electric passenger boats all compete with chronically jammed road bridges. The water is trusted and heavily used. A foiling tier doesn't create demand — it upgrades it, offering speed, smoothness and clean operation over the busiest lagoon crossings, targeting the premium and time-critical segment that today has no fast option.

demand_signals.note: With limited bridges spanning the lagoon, cross-water demand is structurally high — the lagoon is the only relief valve for a city of ~6 million.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire lagoon mesh — Le Plateau↔Treichville/Marcory (~1 nm), Plateau↔Cocody/Riviera (~2 nm), Plateau↔Vridi/Port-Bouët (~6 nm), and runs west toward Yopougon and the lagoon arms — sits far inside the 70 nm all-electric range. Calm, sheltered, flat lagoon water and zero local emissions make this an ideal high-frequency Pioneer II commuter network off existing landings.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The lagoon is pure Pioneer II territory; Quanta-LR hybrid range would open coastal line-haul along the Gulf of Guinea (toward Grand-Bassam ~18 nm or Jacqueville) without charging build-out, extending beyond the urban lagoon core.

precedents.source: Côte d'Ivoire electric-boat programme / public reporting
precedents.what: Government-backed introduction of modern electric passenger boats on the Ébrié Lagoon
precedents.why_it_matters: Abidjan has already validated electric lagoon transport politically and operationally — a foiling tier is the fast, premium next step on a water network the city is actively modernising.

regulatory_note: Lagoon transport is overseen by the District of Abidjan and the national maritime/lagoon transport authorities, with SOTRA and licensed operators running official services. Côte d'Ivoire's own electric-boat initiative signals strong government appetite for clean lagoon modernisation, making the regulatory environment unusually receptive to a zero-emission foiling tier on established landings.
seasonality: The sheltered Ébrié Lagoon is calm and navigable year-round, giving a weather-stable commuter profile; the two rainy seasons (roughly April–July and October–November) bring heavier downpours but little sea-state disruption on the protected water, so the commuter network runs consistently through the year.
